text:
sam: Heads up — getting KV cache sync failures between inference-worker pods in eu-west GPU pool. Alerts started ~10:12 UTC. Pods report `i/o timeout` connecting to peers on 10.42.x.x:22023. Suspect east-west egress being blocked by a netpol or proxy. Anyone touch ml-ns policies recently?

kevin: Seeing failed heartbeats on node-gpu-3: `dial tcp 10.42.5.32:22023: connect: connection timed out`. Also high retransmits/latency spikes between AZs. :thinking_face:

maria: I tightened egress on ml-ns this morning to lock down external access — might be collateral. Policy name `deny-egress-ml`. Quick excerpt below (applied via kustomize):
```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: deny-egress-ml
  namespace: ml-ns
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - podSelector:
        matchLabels:
          app: api-gateway
    ports:
    - port: 443
      protocol: TCP
```

kevin: Oof — that will drop all pod-to-pod TCP on non-443 ports. Can you `kubectl get netpol -n ml-ns` and paste the full name?

maria: Yep, it's `deny-egress-ml`. I scoped it badly. Sorry — thought we were only restricting outbound to external APIs. :grimacing:

sam: KV sync uses TCP 22023 between peers. It also opens ephemeral health/heartbeat ports ~60000-60010 for quick probes. RDMA (RoCE) traffic for some GPU workloads touches host interfaces too — worth keeping hostNetwork/udp ranges in mind. For a quick mitigation we should allow podSelector for inference-worker on 22023.

kevin: Applying temp allow now. Command: 
```bash
cat <<EOF | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: allow-inference-eastwest
  namespace: ml-ns
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      role: inference
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - podSelector:
        matchLabels:
          role: inference
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 22023
EOF
```

infra-bot: Deployment ml/inference-worker rolling restart requested by @sam.

maria: Applied `allow-inference-eastwest`. Also added egress entries for ports 22023 and 60000-60010.

sam: Quick connectivity test: `kubectl exec -n ml-ns inference-worker-0 -- nc -vz inference-worker-1 22023` -> now returns `succeeded`. :thumbsup:

kevin: KV sync backlog drained, logs show catch-up ~2m and then steady state. No more `connect: timeout` errors.

maria: I'll open a proper PR to tighten policy but keep explicit podSelector+ports for inference role. Will add a comment about RDMA/MTU and hostNetwork exceptions so we don't accidentally drop RoCE/heartbeat traffic.

sam: Also let's add an alert for >5% pod-to-pod conntrack drops on GPU nodes and a preflight check in the netpol runbook that lists required east-west ports for inference services.

kevin: FYI I noticed the sidecar proxy's iptables `REDIRECT` rule was intercepting some intra-cluster traffic and bumping conntrack entries — bypassing proxy for the pod CIDR improved throughput in our tests. I'll include that in the PR to eng-runtime.

maria: Thanks — will coordinate with eng-runtime before we re-lock the netpol.

sam: Good catch all. Follow-ups: maria -> PR to update netpol + runbook; kevin -> PR for iptables bypass logic; ops -> alert for conntrack drops.

kevin: Marking incident resolved for now, reopening if we see more timeouts. :white_check_mark:
